rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rīb means doubt; the verse shows the preceding challenge addresses the polytheists who were challenged.
rows.anchor: الريب الشك، وهذه الآية تقتضي أن الخطاب المتقدم إنما هو لجماعة المشركين

rows.speaker: يزيد بن قطيب
rows.claim: Yazid ibn Qutayb reads anzalnā, with an added alif.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يزيد بن قطيب: «أنزلنا» بألف.

rows.speaker: جمهور العلماء
rows.claim: The majority take the pronoun in mithlihi to refer to the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: فقال جمهور العلماء: هو عائد على القرآن ثم اختلفوا.

rows.speaker: الأكثر
rows.claim: Most say the challenge is to produce something like the Qur’an in composition, arrangement, and eloquent meanings familiar to its hearers; its unique composition is the inimitable feature, as discerning theorists hold.
rows.anchor: فقال الأكثر من مثل نظمه ورصفه وفصاحة معانيه التي يعرفونها ولا يعجزهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take the likeness to concern the Qur’an’s unseen disclosures, truthfulness, and pre-eternity, making pre-eternity the basis of the challenge.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: من مثله في غيوبه وصدقه وقدمه، فالتحدي عند هؤلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the pre-eternity interpretation, min is extra or explicative of genus; on the first interpretation it is partitive or explicative of genus.
rows.anchor: ومن على هذا القول زائدة، أو لبيان الجنس، وعلى القول الأول هي للتبعيض،

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group refers the pronoun to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: الضمير في قوله من مثله عائد على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، ثم اختلفوا.

rows.speaker: طائفة
rows.claim: One group understands the challenge as producing an unlettered, truthful person like Muhammad.
rows.anchor: فقالت طائفة: من أمي صادق مثله.

rows.speaker: طائفة
rows.claim: Another group says the polytheists were challenged to produce a sorcerer, soothsayer, or poet like Muhammad, by their own characterization.
rows.anchor: وقالت طائفة: من ساحر أو كاهن أو شاعر مثله. على زعمكم أيها المشركون.

rows.speaker: طائفة
rows.claim: A further group refers the pronoun to the earlier scriptures: Torah, Gospel, and Psalms.
rows.anchor: وقالت طائفة: الضمير في مثله عائد على الكتب القديمة التوراة والإنجيل والزبور.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The command means to call for help; Ibn Abbas takes shuhadāʾ as those present to help and support them.
rows.anchor: والشهداء من شهدهم وحضرهم من عون ونصير، قاله ابن عباس.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains it as calling people to attend.
rows.anchor: وقيل عن مجاهد: إن المعنى دعاء استحضار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The view that shuhadāʾ are witnesses who testify that the challengers produced a counterpart is weak.
rows.anchor: والشهداء جمع شاهد، أي من يشهد لكم أنكم عارضتم، وهذا قول ضعيف.

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ takes their shuhadāʾ to mean their idols.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: شهداؤهم يراد بهم آلهتهم.

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators understand “if you are truthful” to mean truthful in what they said about their doubt.
rows.anchor: أي فيما قلتم من الريب. هذا قول بعض المفسرين.

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that they must be truthful in claiming they can produce a comparable passage.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: فيما قلتم من أنكم تقدرون على المعارضة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative reading is supported by the polytheists’ claim elsewhere that they could produce something like the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: ويؤيد هذا القول أنه قد حكى عنهم في آية أخرى: لو نشاء لقلنا مثل هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In in lam tafʿalū, in precedes lam because lam tafʿalū means they left the act undone; in does not affect the equivalent of a past-tense verb.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: فإن لم تفعلوا، دخلت «إن» على لم لأن لم تفعلوا معناه تركتم الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafʿalū is jussive after lam; lam takes the jussive because, like prohibitive lā, it negates, deleting the verb’s ending as lā deletes a noun’s tanwin.
rows.anchor: وتفعلوا جزم ب لم، وجزمت ب لم لأنها أشبهت «لا» في التبرية في أنهما ينفيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lan normally makes a verb subjunctive, though Abu Ubayda reports that some Arabs use it jussively; the Nābigha verse and Ibn Umar dream report illustrate the usage.
rows.anchor: ومن العرب من تجزم بها، ذكره أبو عبيدة، ومنه بيت النابغة على بعض الروايات:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The categorical prediction stirs their resolve, making their later inability more striking, and reports unseen knowledge before it occurred.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله: لن تفعلوا إثارة لهممهم وتحريك لنفوسهم، ليكون عجزهم بعد ذلك أبدع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Guard yourselves from the Fire” is a command to believe and obey God, phrased as a warning.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: فاتقوا النار، أمر بالإيمان وطاعة الله خرج في هذه الألفاظ المحذرة.

rows.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن، مجاهد، طلحة بن مصرف، أبو حيوة
rows.claim: The majority read waqūduhā with fatḥa; al-Hasan, Mujahid, Talha ibn Musarrif, and Abu Haywa use ḍamma throughout the Qur’an, except Talha exempts its occurrence in al-Buruj.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بن أبي الحسن ومجاهد وطلحة بن مصرف وأبو حيوة: «وقودها» بضم الواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥa, waqūd means fuel or firewood; with ḍamma it means kindling, though both forms are attested for both senses.
rows.anchor: وبفتح الواو هو الحطب وبضمها هو المصدر، وقد حكيا جميعا في الحطب وقد حكيا في المصدر.

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni explains the ḍamma reading by an omitted noun, “possessor of fuel,” since a verbal noun cannot be people; fatḥa for the verbal noun is anomalous, while ḍamma is the normal pattern.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جني: «من قرأ بضم الواو فهو على حذف مضاف تقديره ذو وقودها، لأن الوقود بالضم مصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “People” is grammatically general but specifically means those decreed to enter the Fire.
rows.anchor: وقوله: الناس عموم معناه الخصوص فيمن سبق عليه القضاء بدخولها.

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says the stones are sulfur; they add five torments: quick ignition, foul smell, abundant smoke, clinging to bodies, and intense heat when heated.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن مسعود في الحجارة أنها حجارة الكبريت وخصت بذلك لأنها تزيد على جميع الأحجار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Prepared” refutes those who say the Fire has not yet been created; Ibn Atiyya names the Andalusian Mundhir ibn Said al-Baluti as having fallen into that view.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله تعالى: أعدت رد على من قال: إن النار لم تخلق حتى الآن، وهو القول الذي سقط فيه منذر

rows.speaker: بعض المتأولين
rows.claim: Some interpreters say the Fire described with stones is specifically for unbelievers, while sinners have another Fire.
rows.anchor: وذهب بعض المتأولين إلى أن هذه النار المخصصة بالحجارة هي نار الكافرين خاصة، وأن غيرها هي للعصاة.

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority take this as the Fire generally; mentioning unbelievers intensifies the warning because the addressees act in unbelief, without excluding others from entering it.
rows.anchor: وقال الجمهور: بل الإشارة إلى جميع النار لا إلى نار مخصوصة، وإنما ذكر الكافرين ليحصل المخاطبون

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Abla reads “Allah prepared it for the unbelievers,” adding Allah as the subject and changing the verb form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة: «أعدها الله للكافرين»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first of the previously discussed explanations is preferable: acknowledging prior nonexistence, worldly life, and then death leaves unbelievers no escape from acknowledging the final resurrection.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد رحمه الله: والقول الأول هو أولى هذه الأقوال، لأنه الذي لا محيد للكفار عن الإقرار به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing their initial dead state to themselves as nonexistence, then attributing death to God, strengthens the argument; denial of the later resurrection is unsupported.
rows.anchor: ثم إن قوله أولا كنتم أمواتا وإسناده آخرا الإماتة إليه تبارك وتعالى مما يقوي ذلك القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “to Him” refers to God, meaning return to His reward or punishment; the alternative refers it to resurrection, but the first is clearer.
rows.anchor: والضمير في إليه عائد على الله تعالى أي إلى ثوابه أو عقابه، وقيل هو عائد على الإحياء، والأول أظهر.

rows.speaker: جمهور الناس
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce turjaʿūn with tāʾ ḍamma and jīm fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «ترجعون» بضم التاء وفتح الجيم.

rows.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Ishaq, Ibn Muhaysin, Ibn Yaʿmar, Salam, Fayyad ibn Ghazwan, and Yaʿqub al-Hadrami read the forms with fatḥa on initial yāʾ or tāʾ wherever they occur.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي إسحاق وابن محيصن وابن يعمر وسلام والفياض بن غزوان ويعقوب الحضرمي: «يرجع ويرجعون وترجعون»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kh-l-q means to originate and bring into existence after nonexistence, though it can also describe a person creating something after its initial composition.
rows.anchor: وخلق معناه اخترع وأوجد بعد العدم، وقد يقال في الإنسان خلق بعد إنشائه شيئا، ومنه قول الشاعر:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zuhayr’s line and a second poet’s verse illustrate the human sense of creating after making something or creating what one says.
rows.anchor: ولأنت تفري ما خلقت وبعض ... القوم يخلق ثم لا يفري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “for you” means for reflection, as nearby signs include life, death, creation, and the ordering of the heavens.
rows.anchor: ولكم: معناه للاعتبار، ويدل على ذلك ما قبله وما بعده من نصب العبر: الإحياء،

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some take “for you” to mean that things are permitted and placed in human ownership, supporting presumptive permissibility before revelation.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: بل معنى لكم إباحة الأشياء وتمليكها، وهذا قول من يقول إن الأشياء قبل ورود السمع

rows.speaker: القائلون بالحظر
rows.claim: Those who presume prohibition reject that reading; most make exceptions for necessities such as breathing and movement.
rows.anchor: وخالفهم في هذا التأويل القائلون بالحظر، والقائلون بالوقف، وأكثر القائلين بالحظر استثنوا أشياء

rows.speaker: القائلون بالوقف
rows.claim: Suspension is preferable for a hypothetical case with no revealed evidence or textual attachment; it means exhausting the investigator’s effort on novel cases.
rows.anchor: ويترجح الوقف إذا قدرنا نازلة لا يوجد فيها سمع ولا تتعلق به. ومعنى الوقف أنه استنفاد جهد الناظر

rows.speaker: ابن الصائغ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sa'igh says, as quoted by Ibn Furak, that reason is never without scriptural evidence: a case has a relevant text or established prior state, dispensing with the three-way dispute.
rows.anchor: وحكى ابن فورك عن ابن الصائغ أنه قال: «لم يخل العقل قط من السمع ولا نازلة إلا وفيها سمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jamiʿan is an accusative circumstantial expression.
rows.anchor: ويغني عن النظر في حظر وإباحة ووقف» ، وجميعا نصب على الحال.

rows.speaker: أبو روق
rows.claim: Abu Rawq, as reported by al-Tabari, takes jaʿil to mean “creator”; its taking one object supports the sense.
rows.anchor: وجاعل في هذه الآية بمعنى خالق، ذكره الطبري عن أبي روق، ويقضي بذلك تعديها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada take jaʿil in its sense of “doing” or “making.”
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة: «جاعل بمعنى فاعل»

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet says “the earth” here means Mecca, from beneath which earth was spread; it was where prophets’ peoples were destroyed, and Noah’s, Hud’s, and Salih’s graves lie between the Station and the Corner.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن سابط عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: «إن الأرض هنا يعني بها مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalīfa means one who succeeds another.
rows.anchor: وخليفة معناه من يخلف. قال ابن عباس:

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says jinn preceded Adam, corrupted the earth and shed blood; God sent angels who killed them and drove survivors to sea islands and mountain tops, then made Adam and his descendants successors.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: «كانت الجن قبل بني آدم في الأرض فأفسدوا وسفكوا الدماء فبعث الله

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says Adam’s children are called successors because each generation follows the preceding one; Ibn Atiyya says this can mean a succeeding or succeeded generation.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: «إنما سمى الله بني آدم خليفة لأن كل قرن منهم يخلف الذي قبله

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says Adam is God’s deputy for judging servants by truth and His commands, a role continued by his descendants.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: «إنما معناه خليفة مني في الحكم بين عبادي بالحق وبأوامري»

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads khalīqa with qāf.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي «خليفة» بالقاف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels do not know the unseen or speak ahead of God; the statement that they do not precede Him in speech praises all angels and indicates this is universal.
rows.anchor: وقد علمنا قطعا أن الملائكة لا تعلم الغيب ولا تسبق بالقول، وذلك عام في جميع الملائكة

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر بن الطيب
rows.claim: Qadi Abu Bakr ibn al-Tayyib infers that angels must have had prior information or an indication about the successor’s corruption.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي أبو بكر بن الطيب: «فهذه قرينة العموم، فلا يصح مع هذين الشرطين إلا أن يكون عندهم

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd and others say God had told the angels that the successor’s descendants would corrupt and shed blood, prompting their question.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد وغيره: إن الله تعالى أعلمهم أن الخليفة سيكون من ذريته قوم يفسدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their question may express wonder at God appointing a disobedient creature, at the appointee disobeying despite divine favor, or at both appointment and disobedience.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: فهذا إما على طريق التعجب من استخلاف الله من يعصيه، أو من عصيان من يستخلفه الله في أرضه وينعم عليه بذلك

rows.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى ثعلب
rows.claim: Thaʿlab and others say angels had witnessed the jinn’s corruption and bloodshed, so they asked whether the new successor would follow the jinn’s way.
rows.anchor: وقال أحمد بن يحيى ثعلب وغيره: إنما كانت الملائكة قد رأت وعلمت ما كان من إفساد الجن

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others say God told the angels before this announcement that creatures would corrupt and shed blood; they then asked whether this successor was the one foretold or someone else.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: كان الله تعالى قد أعلم الملائكة أنه يخلق في الأرض خلقا يفسدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Safk ordinarily means spilling blood, but can also describe speaking at length.
rows.anchor: والسفك صب الدم، هذا عرفه، وقد يقال سفك كلامه في كذا إذا سرده.

rows.speaker: جمهور
rows.claim: The majority read yasfiku with kasra on the fāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقراءة الجمهور بكسر الفاء. وقرأ أبو حيوة

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة
rows.claim: Abu Haywa and Ibn Abi Abla read yasfuku with ḍamma on the fāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة

rows.speaker: ابن هرمز
rows.claim: Ibn Hurmuz reads yasfaka in the accusative with wa al-sarf, coordinating one who combines to corrupt and shed blood; al-Mahdawi parses it as an answer to the question, while Ibn Atiyya prefers the first analysis.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن هرمز «ويسفك» بالنصب بواو الصرف كأنه قال: من يجمع أن يفسد وأن يسفك.

rows.speaker: المهدوي
rows.claim: Al-Mahdawi parses the accusative as an answer to the question; Ibn Atiyya prefers the wa al-sarf analysis.
rows.anchor: وقال المهدوي: هو نصب في جواب الاستفهام. قال القاضي أبو محمد: والأول أحسن.

rows.speaker: بعض المتأولين
rows.claim: Some read “while we glorify You” as a question about whether angels should continue in that state or change from it; Ibn Atiyya says this suits a strictly interrogative reading.
rows.anchor: قال بعض المتأولين: هو على جهة الاستفهام، كأنهم أرادوا ونحن نسبح بحمدك الآية، أم نتغير

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others take the words as self-praise and a description of their state, as in Joseph’s “I am a careful keeper, knowledgeable”; Ibn Atiyya says this suits their astonishment at God appointing a disobedient successor.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: معناه التمدح ووصف حالهم، وذلك جائز لهم كما قال يوسف عليه السلام: إني حفيظ عليم

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some understand the angels to mean that if God had appointed them to succession on earth, they would glorify Him; this suits the astonishment reading.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: معنى الآية ونحن لو جعلتنا في الأرض واستخلفتنا نسبح بحمدك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Glorifying God with praise means declaring Him free of what is unfitting to His essence and attributes.
rows.anchor: ومعنى نسبح بحمدك ننزهك عما لا يليق بك وبصفاتك.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masud say the angels’ glorification is their prayer to God.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وابن مسعود: «تسبيح الملائكة صلاتهم لله»

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada takes tasbih in its ordinary linguistic sense: saying “subhan Allah.”
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: «تسبيح الملائكة قولهم سبحان الله على عرفه في اللغة»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bi-hamdika can mean joining praise to glorification; alternatively, it is an interjection: “we glorify and sanctify,” then a submission that God is praised for guiding them to this.
rows.anchor: وبحمدك معناه: نخلط التسبيح بالحمد ونصله به، ويحتمل أن يكون قوله بحمدك اعتراضا

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and others explain “we sanctify for You” as purifying themselves to seek God’s approval; sanctification means purification.
rows.anchor: ونقدس لك قال الضحاك وغيره: معناه نطهر أنفسنا لك ابتغاء مرضاتك، والتقديس التطهير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root means purification, as in “the holy land,” Bayt al-Maqdis, and al-Quds, the thing used to purify.
rows.anchor: والتقديس التطهير بلا خلاف، ومنه الأرض المقدسة أي المطهرة، ومنه بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The yāʾ is omitted from “my people” because vocatives commonly allow deletion and shortening.
rows.anchor: وحذفت الياء في «يا قومي» لأن النداء موضع حذف وتخفيف،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ittikhādhikum is genitive in form but nominative in meaning.
rows.anchor: والضمير في «اتخاذكم» في موضع خفض على اللفظ، وفي موضع رفع بالمعنى،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿijl is an Arabic word for a young cow.
rows.anchor: لفظة عربية، اسم لولد البقرة.

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some say the calf was so named because it was made in haste before Moses returned; Ibn Atiyya rejects this.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: سمي عجلا لأنه استعجل قبل مجيء موسى عليه السلام. قال القاضي أبو محمد

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority say the calf remained gold; al-Hasan says it became flesh and blood, and Ibn Atiyya prefers the majority.
rows.anchor: واختلف هل بقي العجل من ذهب؟ قال ذلك الجمهور وقال الحسن بن أبي الحسن: صار لحما ودما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance means turning from disobedience back to obedience.
rows.anchor: معناه ارجعوا عن المعصية إلى الطاعة.

rows.speaker: جمهور
rows.claim: The majority pronounce the hamza in bāriʾikum and give it kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: «بارئكم» بإظهار الهمزة وكسرها.

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr reads bāriʾikum with a still hamza; Sibawayh’s reported analysis is vowel-shortening, which Ibn Atiyya prefers to full sukun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو: «بارئكم» بإسكان الهمزة. وروي عن سيبويه اختلاس الحركة وهو أحسن،

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad disallows sukun on an inflectional ending amid successive vowels and calls Abu Amr’s reading incorrect.
rows.anchor: وقال المبرد: لا يجوز التسكين مع توالي الحركات في حرف الإعراب، وقراءة أبي عمرو «بارئكم» لحن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya counters that Arabs use sukun on inflectional endings; he cites lines by unnamed poets, Imruʾ al-Qays, Jarir, and Waddah al-Yaman ending in “قوم,” “واغل,” “سويقا,” “المئزر,” “تعرفكم,” and “جلجلان.” Opponents say this removes the ending’s grammatical marker; Abu Ali notes grammarians permit sukun on built endings amid successive vowels.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد عبد الحق رحمه الله: وقد روي عن العرب التسكين في حرف الإعراب، قال الشاعر:

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri reads bāriʾikum as bāriykum, with kasra on the yāʾ and no hamza; this is also reported from Nafiʿ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الزهري «باريكم» بكسر الياء من غير همز، ورويت عن نافع.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada reads fa-iqtālū anfusakum and says it derives from isti qāla; Abu al-Fath analyzes it as iftaʿala with a wāw or yāʾ root, says that weakens Qatada’s etymology, but urges a charitable view of his evidence.
rows.anchor: وقرأ قتادة: «فاقتالوا أنفسكم»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An omitted clause before “then He turned toward you” is understood: “and you did it.”
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: فتاب عليكم قبله محذوف تقديره ففعلتم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Upon you” means upon the survivors: God made the slain martyrs and accepted the survivors’ repentance, forgiving them.
rows.anchor: وقوله عليكم معناه: على الباقين، وجعل الله تعالى القتل لمن قتل شهادة وتاب على

rows.speaker: بعض الناس
rows.claim: Some interpret killing yourselves figuratively as repentance and putting to death the soul’s impulses of desire, obstinacy, and anger, citing the saying about cooking garlic and onion until they die and a line by Hassan.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الناس: فاقتلوا في هذه الآية معناه بالتوبة وإماتة عوارض النفوس من شهوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who said this were the seventy Moses selected; most commentators place their selection after the calf episode to seek forgiveness for Israel, while al-Naqqash and others place it after the sea crossing at the appointed time; Ibn Atiyya prefers the first chronology.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: وإذ قلتم يا موسى يريد السبعين الذين اختارهم موسى، واختلف في وقت اختيارهم.

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators place the seventy’s selection after the calf worship so they could seek forgiveness for the Israelites.
rows.anchor: فحكى أكثر المفسرين أن ذلك بعد عبادة العجل، اختارهم ليستغفروا لبني إسرائيل.

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqash and others instead place the selection when Moses left the sea and sought the appointed meeting; Ibn Atiyya prefers the first account.
rows.anchor: وحكى النقاش وغيره أنه اختارهم حين خرج من البحر وطلب بالميعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says some Israelites who had not worshipped the calf asked Moses to hear God; he was told to choose seventy elders but found only sixty, so ten youths were added and became elders overnight. Six per tribe made 72; Joshua and Talut stayed behind with equal reward. Moses took the seventy after three days’ abstinence and bathing, left Aaron in charge, and brought them to the mountain, where cloud and light came over them and they prostrated.
rows.anchor: وقصة السبعين أن موسى صلى الله عليه وسلم لما رجع من تكليم الله ووجد العجل قد عبد

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqash and others say a cloud covered the seventy, light separated them from Moses, and they fell in prostration.
rows.anchor: قال النقاش وغيره: غشيتهم سحابة وحيل بينهم وبين موسى بالنور فوقعوا سجودا.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi and others report that the seventy heard God command and prohibit, could not bear it, and asked Moses to hear and interpret for them; some later altered what they heard, linked to 2:75. Their faith became unsettled and God tested them with a demand to see Him openly. The request was not intrinsically impossible, though Ahl al-Sunna hold seeing God in this world textually impossible; the thunderbolt burned and killed them in deathlike stillness as a warning.
rows.anchor: قال السدي وغيره: وسمعوا كلام الله يأمر وينهى

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says they died and their spirits departed, then were restored to complete their lifespans; while they lay motionless Moses pleaded that returning to Israel without them would bring ruin and disbelief, since they had left as the best people. Ibn Atiyya clarifies they were good when they departed.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: «ماتوا وذهبت أرواحهم ثم ردوا لاستيفاء آجالهم، فحين حصلوا في ذلك الهمود

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some say Moses thought the seventy were punished for calf worship; this explains his question in 7:155 about destroying them for what the fools did, meaning the calf worshippers.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: بل ظن موسى عليه السلام أن السبعين إنما عوقبوا بسبب عبادة العجل

rows.speaker: ابن فورك
rows.claim: Ibn Furak suggests the seventy were punished for asking Moses to seek vision for them by saying “show us,” something outside his power.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن فورك: يحتمل أن تكون معاقبة السبعين لإخراجهم طلب الرؤية عن طريقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jahratan is a verbal noun used circumstantially; it most apparently attaches to the pronoun in “we see,” though it may attach to “we believe” or “you said.”
rows.anchor: وجهرة مصدر في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jahr means openly, opposite to secrecy; jahara al-amr means that a man made a matter manifest.
rows.anchor: والجهرة العلانية، ومنه الجهر ضد السر

rows.speaker: سهل بن شعيب
rows.claim: Sahl ibn Shuʿayb and Humayd ibn Qays read jahratan with fatḥa on hāʾ; Basrans attest this after an open syllable before a guttural, while Kufans allow it without attestation. Ibn Atiyya also suggests it could be the plural of jāhir, “openly as manifest witnesses.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ سهل بن شعيب وحميد بن قيس: «جهرة» بفتح الهاء، وهي لغة مسموعة عند البصريين

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar and Ali read fa-akhadhatkum al-ṣaʿqa; al-ṣaʿqa is what happens to a person from a thunderbolt, discussed earlier in the sura.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عمر وعلي رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means they looked at their condition; Ibn Atiyya adds the punishment transformed them and took away their sight.
rows.anchor: وتنظرون معناه إلى حالكم. قال القاضي أبو محمد عبد الحق رحمه الله: حتى أحالهم العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God portrays abandoning the afterlife and taking worldly life despite being able to hold to the afterlife as buying the world by selling the afterlife.
rows.anchor: جعل الله ترك الآخرة وأخذ الدنيا مع قدرتهم على التمسك بالآخرة بمنزلة من أخذها

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik applies the exchange image in sales law: one may not buy with a condition allowing selection among units whose individual qualities differ, nor allow unequal exchange in such goods, such as slaughtered partridges.
rows.anchor: وهذه النزعة صرفها مالك رحمه الله في فقه البيوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their punishment will not be lightened in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: ولا يخفف عنهم العذاب في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will receive no help in this world or the next.
rows.anchor: ولا ينصرون لا في الدنيا ولا في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book given to Moses is the Torah; syntactically al-kitāb is the second object of “We gave.”
rows.anchor: والكتاب التوراة، ونصبه على المفعول الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaffaynā derives from qafā, the nape/back: to bring one after another from behind; qafā yaqfū means to follow.
rows.anchor: وقفينا مأخوذ من القفا، تقول قفيت فلانا بفلان إذا جئت به من قبل قفاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The succession resembles God sending messengers in sequence; every messenger after Moses through Jesus affirmed the Torah and commanded adherence to it.
rows.anchor: وكل رسول جاء بعد موسى عليه السلام فإنما جاء بإثبات التوراة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Yahya ibn Yaʿmar read al-rusl with still sīn; Abu Amr does so when a pronoun is attached, such as ruslunā or rusluhum.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ويحيى بن يعمر «بالرسل» ساكنة السين، ووافقهما أبو عمرو إذا انضاف ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bayyināt are proofs given to Jesus; some specify miracles of reviving the dead, healing, and making a bird, others the Gospel, while the verse encompasses all.
rows.anchor: والبينات الحجج التي أعطاها الله عيسى، وقيل هي آياته من إحياء وإبراء وخلق طير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ayyadnāhu means “We strengthened him”; al-ayd means strength.
rows.anchor: وأيدناه معناه قويناه، والأيد القوة

rows.speaker: ابن محيصن
rows.claim: Ibn Muhaysin, al-Aʿraj, and Humayd read āyadnāhu with a lengthened initial vowel.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن والأعرج وحميد «آيدناه»

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and Mujahid read the dāl of al-qudus with sukun; most readers use ḍamma on qāf and dāl, with fatḥa also reported, and Abu Haywa reads with a wāw.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ومجاهد «روح القدس» بسكون الدال. وقرأ الجمهور بضم القاف والدال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Spirit of Holiness is the name by which Jesus used to revive the dead.
rows.anchor: «روح القدس هو الاسم الذي به كان يحيي الموتى»

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the Spirit of Holiness as the Gospel, as God calls the Qur’an a spirit.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: «هو الإنجيل كما سمى الله تعالى القرآن روحا»

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi, al-Dahhak, al-Rabiʿ, and Qatada identify it as Gabriel; Ibn Atiyya says this is soundest, supported by the Prophet telling Hassan that the Spirit of Holiness or Gabriel was with him.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي والضحاك والربيع وقتادة: «روح القدس جبريل صلى الله عليه وسلم»

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabiʿ and Mujahid say al-Quds is a name of God like al-Quddus; the genitive expresses ownership, fitting Gabriel as God’s servant.
rows.anchor: وقال الربيع ومجاهد: القدس اسم من أسماء الله تعالى كالقدوس، والإضافة على هذا إضافة الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations take al-Quds to mean purity or blessing.
rows.anchor: وقيل القدس الطهارة، وقيل القدس البركة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kullamā is an adverb governed by istakbartum; its question form rebukes and demands acknowledgment, while also reporting the Israelites’ conduct.
rows.anchor: وكلما ظرف، والعامل فيه استكبرتم، وظاهر الكلام الاستفهام، ومعناه التوبيخ والتقرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says Israelites killed 300 prophets in a day and reopened their market at its end; another says they killed 70 prophets then sold greens.
rows.anchor: ويروى أن بني إسرائيل كانوا يقتلون في اليوم ثلاثمائة نبي ثم تقوم سوقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in tahwā is part of the relative clause after mā, delayed by the phrase’s length; hawā usually means desire for what is wrong, as here, but can refer to truth.
rows.anchor: وفي تهوى ضمير من صلة ما لطول اللفظ، والهوى أكثر ما يستعمل فيما ليس بحق

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar’s Badr statement shows hawā can refer to sound judgment: the Messenger favored Abu Bakr’s view, not Umar’s.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول عمر رضي الله عنه في قصة أسرى بدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istakbartum derives from kibr, arrogance; farīqan is a fronted object.
rows.anchor: واستكبرتم من الكبر، وفريقا مفعول مقدم.

rows.speaker: جمهور القراء
rows.claim: The majority read ghulf with a still lām, plural of aghlaf like ḥumr and ṣufr; Ibn Abbas says the hearts are sheathed and veiled, not understanding, while Qatada says they are sealed.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جمهور القراء «غلف» بإسكان اللام

rows.speaker: طائفة
rows.claim: A group takes the still-lām form as plural of ghilāf, originally with doubled lām; Ibn Atiyya says this lightened form is rarely used except in poetry.
rows.anchor: وقالت طائفة: غلف بسكون اللام جمع غلاف

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash, al-Aʿraj, and Ibn Muhaysin, with a reading reported from Abu Amr, double the lām; as plural of ghilāf, the hearts are vessels of knowledge needing no knowledge from Muhammad, or the question is how his knowledge could elude them.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش والأعرج وابن محيصن «غلف» بتثقيل اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bal rejects their claim: aversion to belief results from God’s curse for earlier unbelief and wrongdoing, the punishment for their sin.
rows.anchor: وبل في هذه الآية نقض للأول، وإضراب عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qalīlan qualifies an omitted verbal noun, “a little faith they believe”; mā is extra for emphasis, and qalīlan is accusative under yuʾminūn.
rows.anchor: وقليلا نعت لمصدر محذوف تقديره فإيمانا قليلا ما يؤمنون، والضمير في يؤمنون

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to those present in Muhammad’s time; one explanation of “little” is that few believed, as Qatada says.
rows.anchor: والضمير في يؤمنون لحاضري محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation is that their belief lasted only briefly: they anticipated Muhammad before his mission, then disbelieved after it.
rows.anchor: وإما لأن وقت إيمانهم عند ما كانوا يستفتحون به قبل مبعثه قليل، إذ قد كفروا بعد ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation is that only distorted monotheism remained after unbelief: they anthropomorphized God and rejected messengers and Torah, leaving faith too diminished to benefit them.
rows.anchor: وإما لأنهم لم يبق لهم بعد كفرهم غير التوحيد على غير وجهه، إذ هم مجسمون فقد قللوه
